name: Tap
definition: A single press and lift of one finger on a touch surface, the touch equivalent of a click, used to activate a control or select an item.
useWhen: the touch gesture that activates something
notes: Material calls the mechanic touch and the outcome activate; Apple calls it tap.

name: Double tap
definition: Two taps in quick succession on the same spot, conventionally used to zoom in on content or to zoom back out when already zoomed.
useWhen: two quick taps that mean zoom, not activate

name: Long press
definition: A press held in place for a moment before release, used to reveal secondary actions, enter a rearrange mode, or open a contextual menu.
useWhen: holding a touch to reach the secondary action
notes: Long press is the touch counterpart of secondary click; worth a contrastWith edge to context-menu (already on site).

name: Swipe
definition: A quick directional drag of a finger across the screen, faster and coarser than a drag, usually without a specific on-screen target.
useWhen: a fast directional stroke, not a controlled drag

name: Fling
definition: The fastest of the drag family: contact is released while still moving, so the content keeps travelling and the action cannot be dragged back.
useWhen: a throw that releases mid-motion and cannot be taken back

sources.title: Material Design: Gestures (drag, swipe, or fling)

notes: Material distinguishes drag, swipe and fling purely by velocity and whether contact is kept; Apple's word for the same thing is flick.

name: Pan
definition: Moving the viewport across content in any direction while keeping contact, so the content feels anchored to the finger or cursor.
useWhen: moving the view over content rather than the content itself

name: Drag and drop
definition: Picking up an object, moving it under continuous pointer or finger contact, and releasing it over a target that accepts it.
useWhen: moving an object onto a target by holding it the whole way

sources.title: MDN: HTML Drag and Drop API

name: Pinch to zoom
definition: Two fingers moving apart or together on a surface to scale content up or down, with the scale tracking the distance between them.
useWhen: two fingers changing the scale of what is on screen

sources.title: Material Design: Gestures (pinch open and closed)

name: Rotate gesture
definition: Two fingers turning around a common center to rotate the object or view beneath them, the angle tracking the fingers as they orbit.
useWhen: turning content with two fingers rather than a handle

name: Multi-touch
definition: Input from more than one simultaneous contact point, letting a surface distinguish two-finger scrolling, pinching, rotating and larger finger counts.
useWhen: naming input that depends on more than one finger at once
notes: Hard to demonstrate honestly with a single ghost cursor, so demo is none rather than a faked animation.

name: Edge swipe
definition: A swipe that begins off the screen edge and travels inward, reserved by the system for navigation such as going back or revealing a drawer.
useWhen: a gesture that starts at the bezel, not on a control
notes: Relates to drawer, which already exists on the site; edge swipe is the gesture, drawer is the surface.

name: Pull to refresh
definition: Dragging a list past its top edge and releasing to request fresh content, with an indicator that follows the pull and then spins.
useWhen: asking for new content by tugging the top of a list
notes: Android's official name is swipe-to-refresh; the community name is pull-to-refresh. Compose docs call it Pull to refresh.

name: Swipe to dismiss
definition: Sliding an item sideways off its own row or off screen to remove it, where passing a distance threshold commits the removal on release.
useWhen: removing an item by throwing it off its row

name: Swipe actions
definition: Buttons hidden behind a list row that a partial sideways swipe reveals, so destructive or common actions live under the item itself.
useWhen: actions parked behind a row until it is swiped

sources.title: LogRocket: Designing swipe-to-delete and swipe-to-reveal interactions

name: Shake to undo
definition: Physically shaking a device to trigger undo or redo, an accelerometer gesture Apple defines system wide for reversing a recent edit.
useWhen: undo triggered by motion rather than a control

name: Force touch
definition: A press whose depth is part of the input, letting a harder press mean something different from a light one on a pressure sensing surface.
useWhen: press depth carries meaning, not just contact
notes: Largely retired on current hardware, but still the word people reach for; keep as a historical tail entry.

name: Haptic feedback
definition: A brief physical vibration or tap produced by the device to confirm an interaction, mark a boundary, or signal success and failure.
useWhen: feedback the user feels rather than sees or hears

name: Look and pinch
definition: Spatial input where the eyes choose the target and a finger pinch commits the action, so selection and activation come from different body parts.
useWhen: gaze selects, hand confirms, no cursor involved

sources.title: Apple Developer: Explore game input in visionOS

name: Hover
definition: A pointer resting over an element without pressing, a state that exists for mice and pens but has no true equivalent on touch.
useWhen: the pointer is over something but has not committed

name: Hover intent
definition: Waiting out a short delay or watching cursor direction before acting on a hover, so a pointer merely passing through does not open anything.
useWhen: telling a deliberate hover from one passing through

sources.title: Baymard: Provide a hover delay of 300 to 500 ms
NN/g: Timing guidelines for exposing hidden content
CSS-Tricks: Dropdown menus with more forgiving mouse movement paths

notes: Tail gold: the safe triangle and the diagonal problem are separate enough that canonicalize may want them as aliases here or as their own entries.

name: Spring loading
definition: Hovering a dragged item over a container until it opens, so a drag can travel through nested destinations without being dropped and restarted.
useWhen: a drag opens what it hovers so it can go deeper

sources.title: MacPaw: What is spring loading on Mac

name: Peek
definition: A preview shown while a press is held, which either collapses when the finger lifts or commits to the full view if the press continues.
useWhen: a preview that lasts only as long as the press
notes: Merge candidate with hover-card (already on site): peek is the press-held cousin of the hover preview.
resolved: retired 2026-08-18: already an alias of quick-view

name: Pointer capture
definition: Redirecting all events for one pointer to a chosen element, so a drag keeps reaching the control it started on even when it wanders off.
useWhen: a drag must keep its grip after leaving the element

name: Pointer lock
definition: Hiding the cursor and reading only its movement deltas, so input keeps flowing past the edges of the screen instead of stopping at them.
useWhen: input is relative movement, not a screen position
notes: Needs a real user gesture and a browser permission prompt, so it cannot be demonstrated in attract mode.

name: Hit testing
definition: Working out which element sits under a pointer, which decides who receives the event when shapes overlap or transparent areas are in the way.
useWhen: asking which element a click actually lands on

name: Touch target
definition: The activatable area of a control, which needs a minimum size and spacing so a fingertip can hit it without catching its neighbours.
useWhen: sizing what the finger must hit, not what is drawn

sources.title: Smashing Magazine: Accessible target sizes cheatsheet

notes: Sits on the interaction and accessibility border; recorded here because the word is used about input, not about assistive tech.

name: Hit slop
definition: Invisible padding that extends a control's activatable area beyond its drawn bounds, so a small icon can stay small and still be easy to hit.
useWhen: the tappable area is bigger than the visible control

sources.title: Smashing Magazine: Accessible target sizes cheatsheet

name: Fitts's law
definition: The rule that the time to hit a target grows with its distance and shrinks with its size, which is why screen edges and corners are so easy to reach.
useWhen: arguing about how big or how near a control should be

sources.title: Smashing Magazine: Accessible target sizes cheatsheet

name: Drag threshold
definition: The small distance a pointer must travel while pressed before the gesture counts as a drag, so a shaky click is not mistaken for one.
useWhen: deciding when a press turns into a drag

name: Dead zone
definition: A range of input near the resting position that is deliberately ignored, so tiny unintended movement produces no response at all.
useWhen: input near zero is ignored on purpose

sources.title: Apple Developer: Explore game input in visionOS

notes: Game and tool UI vocabulary that has quietly moved into touch UI as the word for ignored micro-movement.

name: Ghost click
definition: A stray click the browser emits after a touch has already been handled, landing on whatever moved under the finger in the meantime.
useWhen: one touch produces a second, unwanted activation

sources.title: FastClick: polyfill to remove click delays
Chrome for Developers: 300ms tap delay, gone away

name: Tap delay
definition: The pause a touch browser once held before dispatching a click, kept open in case a second tap arrived and turned the gesture into a zoom.
useWhen: naming the historic lag between tap and response

sources.title: Chrome for Developers: 300ms tap delay, gone away

name: Secondary click
definition: The alternate pointer press, usually the right button or a two-finger tap, reserved for opening contextual actions rather than activating.
useWhen: the press that asks for options instead of acting
notes: context-menu already exists on the site; secondary click is the input that opens it, worth a seeAlso rather than a merge.

name: Middle click
definition: A press of the scroll wheel button, conventionally used to open a link in a new tab, close a tab, or start autoscrolling.
useWhen: the wheel press, not the left or right button

name: Double click
definition: Two clicks inside a short interval on the same spot, treated as one gesture that opens, edits, or selects a word rather than activating twice.
useWhen: two clicks that mean something a single click does not
notes: Double-click to select a word and triple-click to select a paragraph belong here as aliases unless canonicalize splits them out.

name: Click-through
definition: A click that both focuses an inactive surface and reaches the control underneath, instead of being spent activating the window first.
useWhen: the first click also does the thing, or does not

sources.title: LWN: Focus follows mouse or click to focus?

notes: Also used in CSS sense (pointer-events: none makes an overlay click-through). Two meanings worth disambiguating in the article.

name: Pressure sensitivity
definition: Reading how hard a pen or finger presses, plus tilt and twist, so stroke weight and behaviour vary with the shape of the contact.
useWhen: how hard or how tilted the input is matters

name: Drag handle
definition: The small gripped area, often drawn as rows of dots or lines, that marks where an item may be picked up and dragged.
useWhen: the part of an item that says grab me here
notes: Cross-category: it is a component, but it is discovered through interaction searches. This is the literal what is the word for the little grip dots query.

name: Drop zone
definition: The region that will accept a dragged item, usually highlighted while a compatible drag is in flight so the destination is unmistakable.
useWhen: the area that says a drag can land here

sources.title: MDN: HTML Drag and Drop API

name: Drop indicator
definition: The thin line or gap that appears between items during a drag to show exactly where the item will land if released now.
useWhen: showing the exact slot a drop will occupy
notes: Cross-category: an element, so filed as component, but only ever seen mid-interaction.

name: Drag preview
definition: The translucent copy of the dragged item that follows the pointer, standing in for the original while it stays in place.
useWhen: the ghost of the item that follows the cursor

sources.title: MDN: HTML Drag and Drop API

name: Drag autoscroll
definition: Scrolling a container automatically when a drag is held near its edge, so an item can be moved somewhere currently off screen.
useWhen: a drag needs to reach past the visible area

name: Drag to reorder
definition: Rearranging a list or grid by dragging items to new positions, with the remaining items shifting to open a place for the one in hand.
useWhen: changing order by moving items, not by controls

sources.title: Material Design: Gestures (pick up and move)

name: Momentum scrolling
definition: Content that keeps moving after the finger lifts, decelerating as though it had mass, so one flick can travel a long way.
useWhen: scrolling that coasts after the gesture ends

sources.title: MDN: Basic concepts of scroll snap

name: Rubber banding
definition: Letting content stretch past its scroll boundary under the finger and spring back on release, so the edge is felt rather than hit.
useWhen: the elastic bounce at the end of a scroll

sources.title: Smashing Magazine: Scroll bouncing on your websites

notes: Android's edge glow is the same idea with a different affordance; treat it as an alias unless the article separates them.
resolved: retired 2026-08-18: already an alias of overscroll, which carries "bounce scrolling"

name: Overscroll
definition: Scrolling input that continues after a scroller has reached its limit, which platforms answer with a bounce, a glow, or a handoff to the parent.
useWhen: input keeps scrolling past the end of the content

name: Scroll snap
definition: A scroller that comes to rest on defined positions rather than wherever momentum leaves it, so items always finish aligned.
useWhen: scrolling must settle on items, not between them

name: Scroll chaining
definition: When an inner scroller reaches its end and the gesture continues, the scroll passes to the page behind it unless that handoff is blocked.
useWhen: an inner scroll spills over into the page behind

name: Scroll lock
definition: Freezing the page behind an open overlay so a wheel or swipe moves the overlay's own content and never the document underneath.
useWhen: the page must hold still while an overlay is open
notes: Subject is the document scroller, so this is a genuine iframe case. Pairs with modal-dialog, already on the site.

name: Scroll hijacking
definition: Taking over the page scroller so a gesture drives a scripted sequence instead of moving the page by the amount the reader asked for.
useWhen: the page answers a scroll with something other than scrolling
notes: Pejorative in most usage; the article should say so. Subject is the document scroller, hence iframe.

name: Scroll anchoring
definition: Keeping the reader's position fixed when content loads or resizes above it, by adjusting scroll offset so the visible text does not jump.
useWhen: content loads above and the view must not jump
notes: MDN has a dedicated overflow-anchor page that was not fetched this sweep; verify before authoring.

name: Infinite scroll
definition: Loading the next page of results as the reader approaches the end, so the list extends continuously instead of asking for a next page.
useWhen: the list grows as you reach the bottom of it
notes: Cross-category: filed as pattern, but surfaced by an interaction sweep. Likely also enumerated by the pattern agent.

name: Keyboard shortcut
definition: A key or key combination that runs a command directly, giving practised users a path that skips the menus and the pointer entirely.
useWhen: a command reachable by keys instead of controls

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

name: Chorded shortcut
definition: A shortcut whose keys are held down together like a chord, in contrast to one typed as a sequence of separate presses.
useWhen: keys pressed together rather than one after another

name: Key sequence
definition: A shortcut typed as an ordered run of presses, where the first key opens a mode and the next chooses within it.
useWhen: shortcuts typed in order, like a prefix then a letter

name: Modifier key
definition: A key held to change what another input means, so the same click or keystroke can copy instead of move, or add instead of replace.
useWhen: a held key changes what the next input does

name: Access key
definition: A single letter, usually shown underlined, that jumps straight to a menu or control once the access modifier is held.
useWhen: the underlined letter that reaches a menu item
notes: Windows calls it an access key, general HCI literature calls it a mnemonic; keep both as aliases.

name: Roving tabindex
definition: A focus technique where only one item in a group is in the tab order and arrow keys move that position, so Tab enters and leaves the whole group once.
useWhen: a group of controls that Tab treats as one stop

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

notes: Cross-category candidate with accessibility; the accessibility sweep may also propose it. aria-activedescendant is the sibling technique and could be its own tail entry.

name: Tab order
definition: The path keyboard focus follows through a page as Tab is pressed, which should match the reading order and never strand the user.
useWhen: the order the keyboard walks through a page

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

notes: Cross-category: filed accessibility. Subject is the document's own focus order, so it is a genuine iframe demo.
resolved: folded into focus-order, which carries "tab order" and "tab sequence"

name: Typeahead
definition: Jumping to the item that starts with the letters just typed, so a long list can be reached by spelling rather than by arrowing.
useWhen: typing letters to jump within a list

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

notes: Distinct from autocomplete in a combobox, which is already covered by the existing combobox entry; the article should separate them.

name: Key repeat
definition: A held key firing repeatedly after an initial delay, which is how arrow keys scroll and backspace deletes more than one character.
useWhen: holding a key keeps producing the action

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

name: Focus follows mouse
definition: A focus model in which whatever the pointer is over receives keyboard input, without any click to claim it first.
useWhen: keyboard input goes where the pointer is pointing

sources.title: LWN: Focus follows mouse or click to focus?

notes: Click to focus is the opposite model and is recorded here as an alias; canonicalize may prefer it as a contrasting stub.

name: Selection follows focus
definition: A widget where moving focus also selects, so arrowing through tabs or a listbox changes the selection immediately rather than on a second press.
useWhen: arrowing changes the choice, not just the highlight

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

notes: Contrast pair with the existing tabs entry, where automatic versus manual activation is the visible consequence.

name: Keyboard trap
definition: A place keyboard focus can enter but not leave by keyboard alone, stranding anyone who is not using a pointer.
useWhen: focus goes in and cannot be tabbed back out

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

notes: Merge risk with the existing focus-trap entry: focus trap is deliberate and correct in a dialog, keyboard trap is the accidental failure. The two should contrast, not merge.

name: Light dismiss
definition: Closing a transient surface by clicking outside it or pressing Escape, without a dedicated close control being used.
useWhen: clicking away is enough to close something
notes: The native popover attribute names this behaviour directly (auto versus manual); verify the MDN popover page before authoring.

name: Marquee selection
definition: Dragging a rectangle across a canvas or list to select everything it encloses, the border often animating so the region reads as live.
useWhen: selecting many items by dragging a box around them

sources.title: Computer Hope: What is a marquee?

resolved: folded into lasso-selection, which carries "marquee selection"

name: Lasso selection
definition: Selecting by drawing a freehand outline around items, so the boundary can follow an irregular shape instead of a rectangle.
useWhen: selecting an irregular region by drawing around it

name: Range select
definition: Choosing a contiguous run of items by marking one end and holding Shift while marking the other, selecting everything between them.
useWhen: selecting everything between two items at once

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

name: Multi-select
definition: Adding items to a selection one at a time with a modifier held, so choices accumulate instead of replacing each other.
useWhen: picking several items that are not next to each other

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

name: Selection handle
definition: The draggable grip at each end of a touch text selection, used to widen or narrow the range a finger cannot adjust precisely.
useWhen: adjusting a touch selection by its endpoints

sources.title: iOS HIG: Gestures (touch and hold in text)

name: Caret
definition: The blinking marker showing where typed text will be inserted, moved by clicking, by arrow keys, or by dragging on touch.
useWhen: the text insertion marker, not the mouse pointer
notes: Name collision worth calling out: caret also names the small triangle glyph on a dropdown trigger.

name: Marching ants
definition: The animated dashed outline that circles a selection, moving continuously so the boundary reads as active rather than drawn.
useWhen: the crawling dashed border around a selection

sources.title: Computer Hope: What is a marquee?

notes: Cross-category: filed as motion since the animation is the term, but discovered through selection vocabulary.

name: Scrubbing
definition: Dragging a playhead along a timeline to move through media by hand, previewing frames as the position changes rather than waiting for playback.
useWhen: dragging through time to find a moment

name: Scrubby slider
definition: A numeric field whose label can be dragged sideways to change the value, giving a slider's feel without a slider taking up room.
useWhen: dragging a label to change the number beside it

sources.title: John Nack on Adobe: Scrubby sliders and more

notes: Strong tail term: people search for it as the Figma or Photoshop drag-the-label thing without knowing a name.

name: Nudge
definition: Moving or changing a value by one small fixed step with an arrow key, with a modifier switching to a larger step.
useWhen: moving something by exact steps with the keyboard

sources.title: Figma Learn: Adjust alignment, rotation, position, and dimensions

name: Snapping
definition: Pulling a dragged object into exact alignment once it comes within a small distance of a grid, guide, or another object's edge.
useWhen: a drag jumps into alignment near a guide

name: Smart guides
definition: Alignment lines that appear only while dragging, showing which edges or centers the moving object currently lines up with.
useWhen: the guide lines that appear mid-drag
notes: Borderline layout, but the guides only exist during an interaction, so filed here.

name: Radial menu
definition: A menu whose items sit around the point of invocation, so a choice is made by direction and distance rather than by reading a list.
useWhen: a menu chosen by direction from where you pressed
notes: Cross-category: a component, but it is an interaction technique first. Contrasts with the existing context-menu entry.

name: Marking menu
definition: A radial menu that can be answered before it appears: waiting shows the menu, while a confident stroke in the item's direction selects it outright.
useWhen: an expert stroke that skips showing the menu

sources.title: Buxton: User learning and performance with marking menus

name: Mouse gesture
definition: A command issued by the shape of a pointer stroke, usually with a button held, so a movement stands in for a menu choice.
useWhen: a drawn stroke that means a command

name: Orbit
definition: Rotating a camera around a fixed point by dragging, so the scene appears to turn while the subject stays centered.
useWhen: dragging to turn a 3D view around its subject

sources.title: Apple Developer: Explore game input in visionOS

name: Undo
definition: Reversing the last action and returning to the state before it, which is what lets an interface offer actions without confirming every one.
useWhen: letting an action be taken back instead of confirmed
notes: Relates to the existing toast entry, since undo is the classic toast action.

name: Hold to confirm
definition: Requiring a press to be held for a moment before a destructive action commits, with progress shown so the wait is understood as deliberate.
useWhen: a dangerous action guarded by a held press
notes: Contrast pair with the existing alert-dialog entry: both guard a destructive action, one with a dialog, one with time.

name: Pressed state
definition: The look a control takes while it is actually being held down, confirming that the press was received before the action runs.
useWhen: the moment a control is under the finger

name: Ripple
definition: A circular wash that spreads from the point of contact to acknowledge a touch, Material's way of tying feedback to where the finger landed.
useWhen: touch feedback that spreads from the contact point
notes: Cross-category: filed as motion. State layer is Material's current term and may deserve a separate colour entry.

name: Debounce
definition: Waiting until input has stopped for a set moment before reacting, so a burst of keystrokes or clicks produces one response instead of many.
useWhen: waiting for input to settle before responding

sources.title: NN/g: Timing guidelines for exposing hidden content

notes: Recorded as felt behaviour rather than as a coding utility; the demo should show the search field that waits.

name: Throttle
definition: Capping how often a continuous stream of input is acted on, so a response fires at a steady rate instead of on every event.
useWhen: limiting how often a continuous input is answered
notes: Merge candidate with debounce; keep separate only if the article can hold the distinction clearly.

name: Affordance
definition: What an element makes possible for the person using it, such as a surface that can be pushed, dragged, or scrolled.
useWhen: naming what an element allows a person to do

name: Signifier
definition: The visible cue that advertises an affordance, such as a grip texture, an underline, or a shadow that says this can be pressed.
useWhen: the cue that tells you an action is possible
notes: Norman's distinction: affordance is the possibility, signifier is the advertisement of it. Strong contrastWith pair.

name: Microinteraction
definition: A small self-contained loop of trigger, rule, feedback, and result, such as a toggle that flips, buzzes, and settles into its new state.
useWhen: one tiny complete interaction, trigger to feedback
notes: Cross-category candidate with motion; the motion sweep may also propose it.

name: Quasimode
definition: A temporary mode held open by the user, such as a key kept down, so it cannot be forgotten and ends the moment the hold ends.
useWhen: a mode that lasts only while you hold it
notes: Raskin's term. Explains why holding Space to pan is safer than a pan tool you can forget you are in.

name: Dwell activation
definition: Committing an action by keeping a pointer or gaze still on a target for a set time, for input methods that have no click of their own.
useWhen: holding still is the only way to click

sources.title: NN/g: Timing guidelines for exposing hidden content

notes: Cross-category candidate with accessibility: it is a primary input method for people who cannot click.

name: Sticky hover
definition: A hover style that stays applied on a touch device after a tap, because there is no pointer to leave and clear the state.
useWhen: a tapped control stays looking hovered

name: Thumb zone
definition: The arc of the screen a thumb can reach comfortably while holding a phone one handed, which shapes where primary controls belong.
useWhen: placing controls where a thumb can actually reach
notes: Cross-category candidate with layout; recorded here because it is reasoning about input reach, not about grid.

name: Easter egg
definition: A reward hidden behind an action nobody was told about, put there to be found rather than to be used.
useWhen: a hidden extra whose whole value is the surprise of finding it
notes: The concrete half of the 'Humorous / playful UI' wish, filed in interaction rather than pattern so it lands beside the two terms that make it definable. It is hidden-gesture's HONEST INVERSE: that record (pooled and authored in round 24) is the defect, an action with no signifier that the reader needed, and an easter egg is the same mechanism aimed at something the reader never needed, which is why signifier and affordance are the other two edges. The design content is two questions with real answers: it must never be the only route to anything (the accessibility rule, and the reason it is not a hidden-gesture), and one nobody finds is dead code (the discoverability rule, which is what makes the konami code a convention rather than an arbitrary secret). SOURCE CAVEAT worth keeping: catb.org has no working TLS at all, so the Jargon File URL is http and curl over https fails with exit 60, not a 404; do not 'fix' it to https and do not mark it dead. THE VAGUER HALF OF THE WISH IS REFUSED for now, see the notes entry: playful UI, whimsy and delight have no headword with an honest source, and confetti-burst already claims 'delight moment'.
